name: SemProbe-SQL Synthetic RQ1 Pilot
description: SemProbe-SQL is a framework for designed semantic measurement in SQL education: instead of inferring a learner's semantic model solely from a completed query, it constructs executable database instances on which competing semantic hypotheses produce different observable outcomes and uses learner predictions as diagnostic evidence. This record contains the complete reproducibility package for a fully executable synthetic RQ1 pilot evaluating the technical feasibility and failure modes of this approach. The benchmark contains 20 generated SQL tasks spanning four semantic concept regions, with 12 executable SQLite probe instances per task. Synthetic learner agents follow executable modeled semantic hypotheses under controlled response noise, while coherent held-out executable rules are excluded from the model bank and used to stress-test model-class failure and diagnostic aliasing. The archive contains the complete Python/SQLite implementation, frozen experimental configuration, synthetic task generators, learner-response simulation, adaptive probe-selection policies, tests, raw/generated result tables, figures, reference metrics, environment specifications, provenance records, checksums, and scripts for end-to-end reproduction and verification.
